source.title: Diuretic effect of co-administration of furosemide and albumin in comparison to furosemide therapy alone: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
source.source_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective adult comparative trials

extraction_metadata.scope_note: This is a secondary systematic review. Atoms represent the review methods, its own meta-analytic synthesis, risk-of-bias/certainty assessments, limitations, and author conclusions. Cited trial results are not represented as independently verified primary-study evidence. All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review pending independent human review.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review evaluated whether furosemide plus albumin improves diuresis and natriuresis versus furosemide alone and explored factors modifying that effect.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we investigated the efficacy of furosemide and albumin co-administration through an updated meta-analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible studies were prospective adult studies allocating participants to furosemide alone or furosemide plus albumin and reporting urine output or urinary sodium excretion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For inclusion in the systematic review, a study had to meet the following criteria

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors searched PubMed, EMBASE, Medline, and Cochrane through October 18, 2020 without a language restriction.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This database search was last updated on October 18, 2020.

atoms.canonical_statement: Two investigators independently screened records and full texts, with eligibility disagreements resolved by consensus.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Two investigators (T.H. Lee and J.J. Chen) independently evaluated the titles and abstracts

atoms.canonical_statement: Randomized trials were appraised with RoB 2, with a modified RoB 2 approach for crossover trials.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The study quality of any randomized control trials was assessed using the Revised Cochrane Risk-of-Bias tool

atoms.canonical_statement: Cumulative urine-output and urinary-sodium measurements collected over different time intervals were normalized to hourly rates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we analyzed urine output and urine sodium excretion as urine output rate (ml/hour) and urinary sodium excretion rate (mEq/hour)

atoms.canonical_statement: For crossover trials the authors assumed no carry-over or period effects and imputed a within-person correlation coefficient of 0.5 because required paired variance information was not reported.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we then imputed a correlation coefficient of 0.5 to obtain the standard error of within-individual mean difference

atoms.canonical_statement: Study effects were pooled with a random-effects generic inverse-variance meta-analysis; heterogeneity was assessed with I².

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The data from individual studies were pooled using the random effect model.

atoms.canonical_statement: Prespecified/exploratory subgroup variables included index disease, AKI handling, baseline creatinine, baseline albumin, furosemide dose, albumin dose, observation duration, and baseline eGFR; subgroup interaction p<0.1 was treated as a potential effect modifier.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: subgroup analyses were performed by examining whether different treatment effects existed across the following variables

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors used GRADE to assess quality of evidence for the treatment effect.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The quality of evidence for the treatment effect of albumin and furosemide co-administration in this meta-analysis was assessed based on the guidelines of the GRADE Working Group methodology

atoms.canonical_statement: The diuretic outcome was standardized as hourly urine output in mL/hour.

outcome.definition: Urine output standardized to milliliters per hour.

atoms.canonical_statement: The natriuretic outcome was standardized as hourly urinary sodium excretion in mEq/hour.

outcome.definition: Urinary sodium excretion standardized to mEq per hour.

atoms.canonical_statement: Thirteen prospective studies published from 1987 through 2020 were included, comprising 422 participants; nine used crossover designs and four used parallel-group designs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: data for a total of 422 individuals were analyzed

atoms.canonical_statement: Included populations spanned nephrotic syndrome, liver cirrhosis, unspecified hypoalbuminemia, and critically ill ICU patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The population studied included patients with nephrotic syndrome, liver cirrhosis, hypoalbuminemia of unspecified cause and critically ill (ICU) patients.

atoms.canonical_statement: The search identified 412 records before deduplication; 327 were screened, 23 full texts were assessed, 10 were excluded, and 13 studies were included.
Furosemide plus albumin increased hourly urine output by a pooled mean difference of 31.45 mL/hour versus furosemide alone (95% CI 19.30 to 43.59), with high heterogeneity (I²=87%, p<0.01).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: increased the mean urine output rate to 31.45 ml/hour (95% CI, 19.30–43.59) above that with furosemide treatment alone

atoms.canonical_statement: Furosemide plus albumin increased hourly urinary sodium excretion by a pooled mean difference of 1.76 mEq/hour versus furosemide alone (95% CI 0.83 to 2.69), with high heterogeneity (I²=92%, p<0.01).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: increased the mean urinary sodium excretion rate to 1.76 mEq/hour (95% CI, 0.83–2.69) above that with furosemide treatment alone

atoms.canonical_statement: Four included studies were judged to have high overall risk of bias: Akcicek 1995, Inoue 1987, Nakamura 2013, and Mahmoodpoor 2020.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Overall, four of the included studies were considered to have high risk of bias

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors reported no significant funnel-plot asymmetry for either pooled outcome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Publication bias was assessed by funnel plot and no significant asymmetry was detected

atoms.canonical_statement: For urine output, excluding the Hsu 2006 outlier reduced I² from 87% to 69% while the combination effect remained statistically significant.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the statistical heterogeneity was reduced from 87% to 69%

atoms.canonical_statement: After crossover studies were excluded, only three parallel trials remained and the urine-output analysis showed only a trend favoring combination therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: only three studies were included in the subsequent sensitivity analysis, and that analysis revealed only a trend toward improved urine output rates

atoms.canonical_statement: The natriuretic benefit remained in sensitivity analyses excluding crossover studies, outliers, or high-risk-of-bias studies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There was still benefit from albumin and furosemide co-administration after excluding the studies with crossover designs and excluding outlier studies or studies with high risk of bias

atoms.canonical_statement: Supplementary GRADE assessment rated the diuretic-effect evidence as low certainty because of serious risk of bias, inconsistency, and imprecision; the summary estimated 31.45 mL/hour higher urine output (95% CI 19.3 to 43.59).

atoms.canonical_statement: Although urine output increased, the authors stated that whether co-administration resolves edema remains uncertain; only one included study reported body-weight reduction.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: its efficacy in resolving edema is still indefinite

atoms.canonical_statement: The total patient sample was limited and statistical heterogeneity was high across populations, baseline characteristics, and treatment regimens.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The total number of patients included was still limited, and there was high statistical heterogeneity

atoms.canonical_statement: Albumin and furosemide doses and formulations varied, and most studies did not standardize treatment to body weight.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There was diversity in the doses and types of albumin supplement and furosemide treatment used

atoms.canonical_statement: Several crossover studies lacked albumin measurements after washout and before each intervention, so carryover related to serum albumin could not be excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: some of them did not provide the average albumin level after the washout phase and before each intervention

atoms.canonical_statement: Some studies did not record factors that could influence diuretic response, including salt restriction, NSAID use, and probenecid use.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Data on other factors that might have influenced the diuretic effects were not recorded

atoms.canonical_statement: The 60-mg furosemide subgroup cutoff was partly chosen to split studies evenly and partly treated as a 1 mg/kg stress dose under an assumed 60-kg body weight.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We choose 60mg furosemide as the cutoff point for subgroup analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: Excluding crossover trials left only three parallel-design trials for sensitivity analysis, limiting robustness.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: remaining only 3 enrolled trials with parallel design

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that furosemide plus albumin might enhance diuresis and natriuresis, particularly when baseline albumin is <2.5 g/dL, but high heterogeneity and limited enrollment warrant further parallel randomized trials.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Co-administration of furosemide with albumin might enhance diuresis and natriuresis effects than furosemide treatment alone but with high heterogeneity in treatment response.
